summary: Converts POP, SOP, or CHOP point/line sources into high-sample-rate x/y/color channels suitable for laser projector output.
key_concepts: Generates laser projector drive channels from POP, SOP, or CHOP point/line sources at high sample rates, typically 10000 to 96000 samples per second.
CHOP sources must provide x and y channels; id groups samples into shapes, while additional channels are interpreted as color channels for blanking and diode control.
SOP and POP sources use position, color, and laser-specific point attributes such as LasCorner and corner-hold attributes.
Corner points and guide points control interpolation, repeated hold points, and image sharpness around abrupt direction changes.
Blanking delay, blanking step size, and color timing controls compensate for mirror movement and help avoid visible tails between shapes.
Laser CHOP output routes to Laser Device CHOP for ILDA devices or to Audio Device Out CHOP for supported AVB laser hardware.

common_gotchas: Laser output is physically dangerous; generated plans should require user-side safety/legal/operator review before live output.
CHOP input must provide x and y channels; optional id groups points into shapes and color channels drive blanking/color.
Typical output rates are very high, often 10000 to 96000 samples per second, so sample count and cook cost matter.
The default update method waits until all points are drawn; Every Frame can cause flicker if the source changes faster than drawing completes.
For ILDA hardware routing, send Laser CHOP output to Laser Device CHOP; for AVB audio-based devices, route through Audio Device Out CHOP.
This operator replaces the legacy Scan CHOP.
